moat_against: ROIC fell to 8.7% in 2024 and 2025 (from 21.2% in 2021) — at/below cost of capital through the recent cycle
Gross margin compressed 20.0% (2021) to 14.0% (2025) — limited pricing power
Customer concentration: top 10 customers ~72% of sales (2024), Apple and Qualcomm the largest
ASE is larger; TSMC can insource advanced packaging (CoWoS) — Amkor is partly an overflow/second source
Extreme capital intensity: 2026 capex guided $2.5-3.0B vs ~$1.1B FY2025 operating cash flow
moat_for: #2 global OSAT scale (~$6.7B FY2025 revenue) with advanced-packaging technology (HDFO, 2.5D, co-packaged optics)
Scarce US advanced-packaging footprint: Arizona campus under a 10-year TSMC agreement, multi-year NVIDIA partnership, CHIPS-aligned
Deep, long-tenured relationships with leading fabless customers; qualification/switching friction in advanced packages
moat_justification: World #2 OSAT with real advanced-packaging capability (HDFO, 2.5D) and scarce US capacity (Arizona campus, 10-yr TSMC agreement, NVIDIA partnership), but the economics say weak moat: ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) fell from 21.2%/20.4% in 2021/22 to 9.5%/8.7%/8.7% in 2023/24/25 — at or below cost of capital — and gross margin compressed from 20.0% (2021) to 14.0% (2025). Pricing power is limited against concentrated, powerful customers and a larger rival (ASE); TSMC insourcing is a standing threat.
name: Amkor Technology, Inc.
one_liner: Weak-moat (4/10) cyclical OSAT in a capex supercycle — at $41.82 it does not clear 15% on owner's earnings (weighted IRR 5.6%, weighted IV@15% $10.38; even the super-bull case yields only 9.0%); it would need to trade near $10.38 to clear the 15% hurdle on this method.
